DwG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 40 s. 2022 May 19, 2022 MS. MINDEE MAE SALAZAR mindeemaes@qmail.com Dear Ms. Salazar: This has reference to your e-mail dated April 6, 2022 regarding the following queries: I. Whether the use ofa barangay or municipal owned vehicle in transporting voters to and from the venue of election of director or board member of Batangas Electric Cooperative is allowed and considered for public purpose? 2. Whether it will matter if the incumbent mayor and one of the official candidate running as Director are relatives by affinity? 3. Is PD 1445 otherwise known as Government Auditing Code of the Philippines, Section 4, applicable? As to the first query, the use of a barangay or municipal-owned vehicle in transporting to and from the venue of election for director or board member of an electric cooperative is deemed allowed and considered for public purpose if the same is not imbued with partiality with support towards another candidate for the directorship or board membership in the electric cooperative. If the use of said vehicles is to provide constituents with transportation during the election without any condition in favorable to any of the candidates, the same is deemed a public service. On the second query, the answer will still depend on the presence or absence of bias and/or partiality towards any candidate. As such, if the same is done in the service of the constituents and with observance of utmost impartiality, the fact of relationship by consanguinity or affinity of the incumbent Mayor with the candidates for directorship or board membership in the electric cooperative will not matter. The same will fall within the general welfare provision of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", under Section 16 thereof. Thus, based on the foregoing discussion, the answer to the third query on whether or not Section 4 of PD No. 1445 is applicable, is in the affirmative. Section 4 (2) of said Presidential Decree provides that "xxx (g)overnment funds or property shall be spent or used solely for public purposes". Considering that the controversy involves the use of a vehicle which is a government property, the provision is applicable to the effect that utilization for public purpose is determinant on whether said utilization is proper or not. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No: 8876-34-54

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MAR INGAN Underse etary for Local Government LLLS/RPB/LRALLD/kbm copy furnished: DIRECTOR ARIEL O.
